<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916086_theRebbe_759" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916086_theRebbe_759__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the four effects of Torah study for its own sake correspond to the four worlds Atzilus, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, and that the one who studies in this manner draws from a level above all worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the four actions performed through engaging in Torah study for its own sake, which are enumerated in the Gemara there</t>
    <t s="2">(and particularly as emphasized in the maamar at its beginning: "and it enumerates here four matters"),</t>
    <t s="3">can be said that these four matters correspond to the four worlds ABY"A,</t>
    <t s="4">and correspond to the four divisions of the Sefiros</t>
    <t s="5">(as is known,</t>
    <t s="6">that the ten Sefiros are generally divided into four — corresponding to the four letters of Havayah and corresponding to the four worlds),</t>
    <t s="7">and the matter of one who engages in Torah for its own sake, who brings about these four matters, is a level that is above the four worlds,</t>
    <t s="8">therefore he affects them.</t>
    <t s="9">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="10">that it is known that Beriah is the aspect of Chabad,</t>
    <t s="11">Yetzirah is the aspect of Chagat,</t>
    <t s="12">and Asiyah is the matter of the garments from Malchus and the kings of the lower ones,</t>
    <t s="13">and higher than that,</t>
    <t s="14">is the aspect of Nehi.</t>
    <t s="15">However, Atzilus is the world of unity,</t>
    <t s="16">meaning that even from the perspective of the vessels it is the world of unity,</t>
    <t s="17">as is known that in Atzilus, He and His life are one, and also He and His limbs are one.</t>
    <t s="18">And this is that the four matters mentioned above correspond to the four worlds ABY"A — "makes peace in the retinue" etc., which is the matter of the midos as mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="19">the aspect of Chagat,</t>
    <t s="20">Yetzirah.</t>
    <t s="21">"Builds palaces" etc., which is the matter of the mochin as mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="22">Beriah.</t>
    <t s="23">"Protects the entire world" etc.,</t>
    <t s="24">the actual conduct in the world that comes from the aspect of the mochin and the midos,</t>
    <t s="25">the aspect of Nehi and Malchus and the kings of the lower ones,</t>
    <t s="26">Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="27">"Brings the redemption closer," which is the matter of the perfection that is above the matter of creation as mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="28">the aspect of Atzilus, the world of unity.</t>
    <t s="29">And this is that in the explanation in the maamar regarding "brings the redemption closer," it is written that it is changed in its very essence for good,</t>
    <t s="30">because in Atzilus, evil does not dwell.</t>
    <t s="31">However, the matter of one who engages in Torah for its own sake, who brings about these four matters, is above even the world of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="32">as mentioned above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the concept to the maamar explaining the aspect of "Akudim in a single vessel," which is the encompassing level of Atzmus Ein Sof that is above division and equal in all worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And one can connect this with what is explained in the maamar beginning "To understand what is said in Etz Chaim of the Alter Rebbe"</t>
    <t s="2">(which was said on Yud-Tes Kislev),</t>
    <t s="3">where it explains there the matter of the aspect of Akudim in a single vessel,</t>
    <t s="4">which is the aspect of Kesser etc.,</t>
    <t s="5">the general encompassing level that is above division,</t>
    <t s="6">therefore it includes all the Sefiros equally.</t>
    <t s="7">For in general, it is the aspect of the Essence of Ein Sof that illuminates in all worlds equally.</t>
    <t s="8">And as is explained in the maamar there,</t>
    <t s="9">that this is why even infants and women say regarding the Essence of Ein Sof "You are present,"</t>
    <t s="10">because from the perspective of the Essence of Ein Sof, all are equal,</t>
    <t s="11">and the difference is only in the aspect of revelation,</t>
    <t s="12">but from the perspective of the aspect of concealment, all are equal etc.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is the matter of one who engages in Torah for its own sake,</t>
    <t s="14">that through engaging in Torah for its own sake, he draws down the aspect of the encompassing level mentioned above, which is above worlds,</t>
    <t s="15">and therefore he affects all four worlds.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section adds explanation that the maamar is a foundational one outlining the entire order of Hishtalshelus, first explaining the general concept of lights and vessels, then detailing it from below to above and from above to below.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And one may add explanation in the aforementioned maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">and as an introduction,</t>
    <t s="3">that this maamar is a foundational maamar that explains the entire order of Hishtalshelus,</t>
    <t s="4">except that it explains the matter with extreme brevity,</t>
    <t s="5">and as our sages said,</t>
    <t s="6">"A person should always teach his student in a concise manner."</t>
    <t s="7">And this is also the order of the matters in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="8">that at the beginning of the maamar it explains the general matter of lights and vessels,</t>
    <t s="9">and afterwards it explains in detail,</t>
    <t s="10">first as it is from below to above,</t>
    <t s="11">and then as it is from above to below.</t>
    <t s="12">For,</t>
    <t s="13">at the beginning of the maamar it explains the general matter of lights and vessels</t>
    <t s="14">[and it is noteworthy,</t>
    <t s="15">that in the manuscript</t>
    <t s="16">it was first written: "The matter of lights and vessels above,"</t>
    <t s="17">and afterwards he crossed out the word "above"],</t>
    <t s="18">that the lights, in and of themselves, are in the aspect of concealment,</t>
    <t s="19">and the matter of revelation is specifically through the vessels.</t>
    <t s="20">And he explains this through a parable from the soul of man,</t>
    <t s="21">"From my flesh I perceive" etc.,</t>
    <t s="22">that the faculties of the soul, in and of themselves, are in concealment,</t>
    <t s="23">and only through their enclothing in the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="24">then they come into revelation.</t>
    <t s="25">Therefore, when a person's soul is reincarnated into the bodies of the mineral, vegetable, and animal, it is in concealment,</t>
    <t s="26">because they are not suitable vessels,</t>
    <t s="27">and likewise in man himself, when the intellect enclothes in a limb other than the brain,</t>
    <t s="28">it is in concealment.</t>
    <t s="29">And likewise above,</t>
    <t s="30">that the revelation of the ten Sefiros is specifically through the vessels,</t>
    <t s="31">but the lights, in and of themselves, are in the aspect of simplicity and concealment.</t>
    <t s="32">And after he explains the general matter of lights and vessels,</t>
    <t s="33">he continues to explain the matter as it is from below to above,</t>
    <t s="34">and as it is from above to below.</t>
    <t s="35">First he explains the matter from below to above,</t>
    <t s="36">namely,</t>
    <t s="37">that the intellect in the soul of man is generated from the aspect of the vessels of Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="38">and likewise the lights of Asiyah are drawn from the aspect of the vessels of Yetzirah,</t>
    <t s="39">and so it is in the entire order of Hishtalshelus,</t>
    <t s="40">that the aspect of the lights in each world are drawn from the aspect of the vessels of the world above it.</t>
    <t s="41">And afterwards he explains the matter from above to below,</t>
    <t s="42">namely,</t>
    <t s="43">that the vessels of Atzilus become Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah for BY"A.</t>
    <t s="44">From the aspect of the ten inner vessels,</t>
    <t s="45">the aspect of Chabad,</t>
    <t s="46">becomes the aspect of Neshamah for Beriah,</t>
    <t s="47">from the aspect of the ten middle vessels,</t>
    <t s="48">the aspect of Chagat,</t>
    <t s="49">becomes the aspect of Ruach for Yetzirah,</t>
    <t s="50">and from the aspect of the ten outer vessels,</t>
    <t s="51">the aspect of Nehi,</t>
    <t s="52">becomes the aspect of Nefesh in Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="53">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="54">that in each world</t>
    <t s="55">(of the three worlds BY"A)</t>
    <t s="56">there exist the three aspects of Chabad, Chagat, and Nehi,</t>
    <t s="57">only that the world of Beriah is primarily Chabad,</t>
    <t s="58">the world of Yetzirah is primarily Chagat,</t>
    <t s="59">and the world of Asiyah is primarily Nehi.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
